name: What a Hunter Leaves

levels.entry: Somebody walks ahead of the herd carrying a short bow, and comes back with nothing most days.
The bow is timber with sinew glued along the back and antler let into the tips. Short enough to draw on a slope.
When something is taken it is one animal, and it is old or lame. I asked how that is decided and was told you learn to tell, which is not an answer I can write down.
Nothing is left. Hide, sinew, long bones, gut -- and the antler was not taken at all, it was picked up in spring where it fell.
So the bow is sinew, and sinew is skinning, and the bow is what makes the skinning possible. It goes round. They know it goes round; it came up before I raised it.

notes: The ethic of taking, given to a person rather than stated as a rule. The materials layer has hide, sinew, tusk and bone all `won_from` living animals, and the game hands them over as easily as a reed. This is the one place the cost is said out loud, and it is said by somebody who does it rather than by somebody objecting.
